issues.description: Template dd.py defines UniqueTable.__init__(self, size: int) but the module later instantiates UT = UniqueTable() without providing the required size argument. This is a self-contradiction in the template that will raise a TypeError on import and block students from running or developing against the provided template. The solution repository uses a no-argument UniqueTable.__init__ (i.e., UniqueTable()) which indicates the intended design is a parameterless constructor. The mismatch between the constructor signature and its usage in the template (and the difference from the solution) is a structural error rather than an intentional pedagogical omission.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template UniqueTable constructor signature match its usage and the solution. Either change UniqueTable.__init__ to a no-argument constructor (def __init__(self) -> None:) as in the solution, or, if a size parameter is required, update the instantiation UT = UniqueTable() to pass a sensible size (e.g., UT = UniqueTable(size)). Prefer the no-argument constructor to align with the solution and avoid blocking students.

issues.description: The UniqueTable constructor signature differs between the template and the solution. In the template dd.py the UniqueTable.__init__ is defined to accept a 'size' parameter, but later in the same file UT = UniqueTable() is called with no argument. In the solution dd.py the UniqueTable.__init__ takes no parameters. This mismatch (constructor parameter present vs. absent) creates an API/identifier inconsistency for the same conceptual entity (the UniqueTable), which can confuse students about how to instantiate and use the UniqueTable and may cause runtime errors in the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the UniqueTable constructor consistent across artifacts. Either remove the 'size' parameter from the template UniqueTable.__init__ (so it matches the solution), or make the solution constructor accept an optional 'size' (e.g., def __init__(self, size: int | None = None)) and ensure UT = UniqueTable() is valid. Update any usages accordingly so the class API is identical in template and solution.
